name: Opus 5 unrestricted
strategy: Concentrated bet on the 2026 oil-supply-shock rotation: ~53% effective energy exposure via 2x ERX plus refiner MPC, carried by low-correlation healthcare/financials/defense longs, hedged by a short in oil-taxed consumer discretionary and a small stopped short-DOGE perp, with 8% cash at 4%.

positions.thesis: Trimmed 24 to 22 — not because the thesis weakened but because I am now expressing part of the same view through MPC, which does not die on the same headline. The crude case got materially better this week: Brent $93.86, a second straight weekly gain, against $88.52 last week, while Trump declared an 'economic D-Day' promising to sanction ANY country that trades with Iran and Bessent details it Monday. That is supply removal, not de-escalation — secondary sanctions strand Iranian barrels that are currently reaching buyers, layered on top of a blockade, a strait still significantly choked six months into the war with no off-ramp, and an IEA Q3 deficit of 1.8 mb/d. XLE at $63.58 has not caught up to what a $94 Brent plus that policy implies, and ERX is 2x that gap. This is still my largest directional risk and the bear case is unchanged and honest: a deal lands, crude gaps down, and the stop gaps through it. Size is the real protection, which is why 22 and not 30. New take-profit at +40%, roughly a 20% XLE move — around $115-120 Brent, the level where demand destruction, SPR politics and pressure on Tehran to settle invert the risk/reward and I would rather be paid than greedy. Stop held at -22%, capping the leg at ~4.8% of NAV.

Trimmed 25 to 20 to fund MPC and silver, not because it stopped working — it hit 'Confirmed Leader' status on 8/7 and is the second-strongest sector behind energy, at ~18x forward with a 0.65-0.75 beta, carried by real Q2 earnings beats and the GLP-1 franchise rather than by defensive flows. It remains the ballast that makes a 2x energy fund carryable, and 20% is still enough of it to do that job. The honest reason for the trim is that a Fed cutting in September into a weak dollar is a regime where low-beta quality compounds steadily but does not lead, and I found two places this week where the same capital has a sharper edge. No stop, unchanged reasoning: this is the position I want to still own if everything else here is wrong, and a stop on my lowest-beta leg would only fire in a market-wide flush, which is the exact moment I want to be holding it.

Held flat at 20 because this week is what I bought it for and adding after a 5.4% weekly run is chasing. Gold printed ~$4,607 on 8/21, up 2% on the day to a three-month-plus high in record territory, on Powell opening the door to a September cut with markets at 91% odds — while he simultaneously kept inflation risks 'tilted to the upside' with tariff pass-through 'clearly visible.' Cutting into sticky inflation with federal debt through $40 trillion and a soft dollar is the exact monetary setup gold is built for, and it is stacked on a Hormuz premium and central-bank buying, so the bid is layered rather than single-source. It also remains the only asset here that wins in both tails of my own book: stalemate keeps the geopolitical bid alongside ERX, and a sudden settlement that kills ERX lands on a labor market that shed 23,000 jobs and a Fed already cutting. Still bullion rather than GDX — mining operating leverage on top of a 2x energy fund would concentrate variance in the one thing I am trying to reduce. Stop tightened -13% to -12%, capping the leg at 2.4% of NAV: still far outside any headline shakeout, but a 12% break from a record would mean the rate-cut repricing died, and at that point this has stopped hedging.

New 12% position, and the most important change I made. Refining margins are not a crude-price bet, they are a product-scarcity bet, and the scarcity just went to records: the US 3-2-1 crack spread hit ~$64/bbl and the diesel crack hit $99.125/bbl, up 264% year over year, on a structural global refining-capacity shortage compounded by Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and reduced fuel exports. MPC's own refining and marketing margin went from $17.58 to $36.33 per barrel and industry margins have nearly tripled since the start of 2026 — that is realized cash, not a forecast. The reason this earns a place next to ERX rather than duplicating it is the divergence in the tail I actually fear: if a Hormuz deal lands and crude collapses, ERX halves the move twice, but a refiner buying cheaper feedstock into a market that is still physically short distillate keeps or widens its crack — earlier this year products stayed elevated through exactly that kind of crude pullback. Unlevered equity at 2bps, no leveraged-ETF decay, and it pays a dividend while I wait. Entering near an all-time-high close ($365.21 on 8/18, $358.23 on 8/20) is the cost of the setup; the risk is that record cracks mean-revert as capacity or demand adjusts, which is why this is 12 and not 20. Stop -18% caps the leg at ~2.2% of NAV.

Held at 10% — both drivers strengthened again and this is the natural pair to a record distillate crack. The cost side is now brutal and confirmed by the industry itself: the global airline sector has nearly HALVED its 2026 profit forecast citing Middle East fuel costs, US carriers' fuel bill ran ~$6.7bn in May at +85% y/y, jet fuel sits in the record-crack complex I just went long via MPC, and carriers are cutting unprofitable routes and grounding less fuel-efficient aircraft — that is management telling you the margin math no longer works. Brent went from $88.52 to $93.86 this week, so the pressure is still increasing, not peaking. The demand side is independent and intact: a contracting labor market with leisure and hospitality specifically soft reads directly on discretionary air travel, and discretionary leisure flinches first as fares rise to cover fuel. Portfolio-wise this is my only equity hedge with the index at records. I am naming the concentrated failure mode rather than hiding it: a Hormuz deal costs me on ERX and this leg simultaneously, though MPC now blunts that. Squeeze risk stays specific — the $2.5bn Frontier/Avelo federal liquidity ask with a possible government equity stake. Borrow at 3% APR on 10% is ~30bps a year. Stop -18% caps it at 1.8% of NAV; take-profit held at +25%.

Raised 7 to 10 because the catch-up I was sized small for waiting on finally started. Silver ran to $69.87, up ~3% Friday and ~8.8% on the week against gold's 5.4%, pulling the gold/silver ratio to ~65.9 from 67.22 — the compression is now accelerating rather than grinding. Same dovish engine as GLD with more beta: a September cut at 91% implied odds, a weak dollar, and record-territory precious metals. Two things make me want more of it here specifically rather than more gold: silver is still meaningfully below its February mid-$80s high while gold is at a record and BTC just posted its best week since 2024, so this is the laggard expression of the debasement trade rather than the chased one; and a Fed easing into 'clearly visible' tariff inflation supports the industrial half of silver demand that a weakening labor market had been cutting against. It stays 10 and not 20 because that industrial component genuinely cuts both ways and because this metal's own history is violent — mid-$80s to $64 to $70 inside a year. Stop stays wide at -18%, capping the leg at 1.8% of NAV; anything tighter is noise on a chart like this.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Because I found a way to increase energy exposure while REDUCING my worst tail. My single largest risk has always been one headline wide: a Hormuz deal lands, crude gaps down, and a 2x fund halves the move twice over. Refining margins are the one energy exposure that does not share that failure mode — the diesel crack hit a record $99.125/bbl (+264% y/y) and the 3-2-1 hit a record ~$64 on a structural refining-capacity shortage plus Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, and product prices stayed elevated through earlier crude pullbacks precisely because the bottleneck is refining, not crude. So I cut ERX from 24 to 22 and put 12 into MPC: total energy exposure rises from 48% effective to 56%, but the crude-beta share of it falls, and if the deal I fear actually lands, cheaper feedstock into a still-short product market is a partial offset rather than a second loss. Everything else is a modest lean into what verified: Brent $93.86 with Bessent announcing secondary sanctions on every country that trades with Iran on Monday, Powell opening the door to a September cut at 91% market-implied odds, gold at a record and silver finally compressing the ratio. I raised silver 7 to 10 and funded it plus MPC out of an XLV trim and cash. I deliberately did NOT re-add crypto after BTC's biggest week since 2024, and I did not re-short DOGE after being stopped out on 8/20 — both would be chasing.
novelty: This book is not a Round-2 derivative — I run no Round-2 account — and the substantive novelty this week is that my energy risk is no longer a single levered crude-beta expression: adding MPC splits it into a crude-price leg and a refining-margin leg whose payoffs diverge in exactly the scenario that would otherwise blow the book up, while the crypto sleeve is now deliberately empty rather than short.
research_notes:
VERIFIED THIS WEEK (prices through 2026-08-21 close):

OIL / HORMUZ — the thesis strengthened, hard. Brent $93.86 on 8/21 (+5%+ on the week, second consecutive weekly gain), vs $88.52 last week and $61-ish XLE. XLE $63.58 on 8/19 vs $61.06 a week ago. No de-escalation: Trump declared an "economic D-Day," saying ANY country trading with Iran will be sanctioned — the "most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country" — and Bessent holds a press conference MONDAY 8/24 with details, having already committed to the Hormuz blockade plus "the toughest sanctions in history." The war is near its six-month mark with no diplomatic or military off-ramp; the strait remains significantly choked. Secondary sanctions on Iran's buyers is a supply-REMOVAL policy, not a de-escalation, and it lands into an IEA Q3 deficit estimate of 1.8 mb/d.

REFINING — the new information that actually changed my book. US 3-2-1 crack spread hit a record ~$64/bbl; the DIESEL crack hit a record $99.125/bbl, +264% year over year. Marathon Petroleum's refining & marketing margin went from $17.58 to $36.33/bbl; Valero's realized margin roughly doubled y/y; industry refining margins have nearly tripled since the start of 2026. The driver is structural — a global refining capacity shortage, Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, and reduced fuel exports — which is why product prices stayed elevated even on crude pullbacks earlier this year. MPC closed $358.23 on 8/20 against an all-time-high close of $365.21 set 8/18.

MACRO — Powell at Jackson Hole opened the door to a September cut ("the baseline outlook and the shifting balance of risks may warrant adjusting our policy stance"), explicitly citing downside employment risk after the July jobs report. Fed funds futures now price ~91% odds of a 25bp September cut. He kept inflation risks "tilted to the upside" with tariff pass-through "clearly visible" — i.e. cutting into sticky inflation, which is the textbook gold regime.

PRECIOUS METALS — gold $4,600.91-$4,607 spot on 8/21, +2.03% on the day, three-month-plus high and record territory, vs ~$4,371 last week (+5.4% on the week). Silver $69.87, +3% on the day, +8.8% on the week, vs $64.21 last week. Gold/silver ratio now ~65.9 vs 67.22 last week — the catch-up I was waiting on finally started moving. US federal debt topped $40 trillion; dollar weak.

CRYPTO — I verified the market note. BTC $78,335 Friday close, +7.26% on the day and +22% on the week, its strongest weekly run since 2024, highest since May, driven by Treasury long-end buybacks pulling yields down, a weaker dollar, and the largest spot-ETF daily inflow since May (BlackRock took 83% of Thursday's $606m). My DOGE 3x short was stopped out 8/20 at $0.0907 for ~$3.89 back to cash — beta ran it over exactly as I said the risk was. Analysts flag overbought signals into thin weekend liquidity.

AIRLINES — the global airline industry has nearly HALVED its 2026 profit forecast, citing Middle East conflict fuel costs; US carriers' fuel bill was ~$6.7bn in May, +85% y/y; carriers are cutting unprofitable routes and grounding less fuel-efficient aircraft. JETS 12-month range $23.48-$34.06. With the jet/distillate crack at a record, the cost side of my short is now worse for airlines than at any point since I put the trade on.

HEALTHCARE — XLV reached "Confirmed Leader" status on 8/7, +1.60% as of 8/18 and the second-strongest sector behind energy, ~18x forward, beta 0.65-0.75, Q2 beats and GLP-1 franchise growth intact.

WHAT I CONCLUDED: every leg I own is working and the two catalysts ahead (Bessent Monday, September FOMC) both cut my way. The one thing I did NOT do is chase crypto after a 22% week — I already own the debasement trade in a laggard form (silver is still well below its February mid-$80s high while BTC just went vertical), and re-shorting DOGE days after being stopped out in a liquidity-driven melt-up would be revenge trading, not edge.
